early_history_summary: Nishiya began skateboarding at age 5-6 in Matsubara, Osaka, influenced by her older brother Hayate and taught by her father Sho, who studied videos of foreign skateboarders to coach her. She practiced 3-4 hours daily at a local skate park and was ranked 5th in Olympic World Skateboarding rankings before Tokyo 2020.
family_context_summary: Born in Osaka to father Sho and mother Tomomi; father taught her skateboarding by studying videos though he was not a skilled skater himself. She has an older brother Hayate who first inspired her to start skating.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Sho introduced the family to skateboarding and coached Momiji by studying videos of foreign skateboarders, though he was not a domain expert. The family is not documented as having prior skateboarding connections.

milestone_by_age_26: Won silver medal in women's park skateboarding at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 12, becoming the youngest Japanese Summer Olympic athlete ever, and won a second silver at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 15.
early_history_summary: Hiraki started skateboarding at age 5 in Tomakomai, Hokkaido, after her parents took her to a local skate park wanting a family sport. She had no specific coach, instead learning from videos and older skaters at her local park. She was competing by age 7-8 and won the Japanese Skateboarding Championship in 2019 at age 10.
family_context_summary: Born in Kutchan, Hokkaido to father Yosuke (who works at Hokkaido Electric Power) and mother Minako (a homemaker). Her mother drove her daily to practice in Sapporo and accompanied her to US competitions. She has a younger brother Manato who also skateboards.

name: Rayssa Leal
milestone_by_age_26: Won silver medal in women's street skateboarding at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics at age 13, becoming Brazil's youngest-ever Olympic medalist, and won bronze at the Paris 2024 Olympics at age 16.
early_history_summary: Leal started skateboarding at age 6 in Imperatriz, Maranhão, Brazil, after receiving a skateboard as a gift. At age 7, a viral video of her doing a heelflip in a fairy costume was shared by Tony Hawk, earning her the nickname 'Fadinha do Skate' (Skate Fairy). She gained millions of social media followers and made her X Games debut in 2019 at age 11.
family_context_summary: Born in Imperatriz, Maranhão, Brazil to parents Haroldo Oliveira Leal and Lilian Mendes. Family was poor; Leal wrote that her parents could not afford good skateboarding shoes and she walked with shoes that had holes in the soles. She has a younger brother Arthur.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents are not documented as having skateboarding expertise. Both parents had Olympic aspirations in football but did not achieve them. Family was financially constrained, unable to afford quality skateboarding equipment.

Her family was poor and could not afford quality equipment, but the viral exposure and mentorship from Brazilian skateboarding star Leticia Bufoni helped her career. name: Quan Hongchan

She began diving training and joined the Guangdong provincial team in 2018. She trained up to 7 hours daily with 400 dives per day, motivated partly by wanting to earn money to treat her mother's illness from a 2017 car accident. She won the Chinese National Championships in 2020 before her Olympic breakthrough.
